These instructions use my customized `tmux` prefix key, `ctrl-q`. Adapt them if you use a different prefix.

## Move the Pane

1. Focus the pane to move.
2. Press `ctrl-q m` to mark it.
3. Navigate to the destination window and focus the pane where the split should occur.
4. Press `ctrl-q :`, enter `move-pane`, and press Enter.

When no source is specified, `move-pane` uses the marked pane. The focused pane is the destination.

## Choose the Layout

By default, `move-pane` places the panes one above the other. The following options control their placement:

* `-h`: place the panes side by side.
* `-v`: place the panes one above the other.
* `-b`: place the moved pane to the left of or above the destination.
* `-l 40%`: give the moved pane 40% of the available width or height.

### Example

```tmux
move-pane -h -b -l 40%
```

This moves the marked pane to the left of the destination and gives it 40% of the available width.

## Clear the Mark

Press `ctrl-q M` to clear the mark without moving the pane.

Tmux allows only one marked pane at a time. Marking another pane replaces the existing mark.

## Move a Pane by ID

For scripts or precise commands, specify the source and destination pane IDs:

```tmux
move-pane -s %42 -t %17
```

List all pane IDs with:

```tmux
list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id} #{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}'
```

`move-pane` and `join-pane` perform the same operation. `move-pane` is used here because its name describes the intent more clearly.
